description: The National Space Law collection of the United Nations Office for Outer Space Affairs gathers the laws, regulations and policies that States have adopted on the exploration and use of outer space, such as space activities acts, launch and operation licensing rules, space resources acts and collision avoidance guidelines. UNOOSA compiles it from submissions by States, and since 2022 hosts many texts in ASTRO, Accessing Space Treaty Resources Online, a database of national space laws, policies and regulations of the member States of the Committee on the Peaceful Uses of Outer Space. Coverage is worldwide, listed by State from Algeria onward, with external links checked (for example on 16 March 2026). Format and access: free web pages linking to texts in the languages received, some with tentative English translations. Licence: UNOOSA terms of use; texts are reproduced as submitted and not formally edited or translated by the UN. Caveats: completeness depends on what States submit, and external links can break. It gives the regulatory context for modelling satellite operators, launch activity and space infrastructure resilience. Related catalogue records are the UN Register of Objects Launched into Outer Space and the ECSS space engineering standards.
